threads.subject: URGENT-caregiver-bridging open work permits-REP-2017-2075
threads.question:
To whom it may concern,
I write with a question about the open bridging work permit policy, as it relates to caregivers. In the old school LICC, we used to include the open permit extension application with the PR application, and the two would then be processed concurrently. But those work permit applications were being filed on the basis of the R207 LMO exemption provisions.
Now that the LICC has been replaced by the caregiver pathways, the exemption being used is the same one we use for EE applications, and these are typically filed separate from the PR application, and with AOR of the PR application enclosed.
So my question is this – is it possible to apply for PR under the new pathways and either include an open bridging work permit application in that same package, or apply separately but without a letter from IRCC confirming receipt of the PR application (we would include instead a copy of the PR application and proof of filing)? The issue here is that it will take several weeks for us to receive AOR of filing of the PR application, and her work permit is due to expire in less than that period of time.
Thanks in advance for your reply!
Sincerely,
Zare.Atabak
threads.answer:
Hello,
Thank you for contacting the Immigration Representatives inbox. Please see below for the response to your question:
Question: is it possible to apply for PR under the new pathways and either include an open bridging work permit application in that same package, or apply separately but without a letter from IRCC confirming receipt of the PR application (we would include instead a copy of the PR application and proof of filing)?
Response: The applications are submitted separately -first the application for PR, and once the Acknowledgement of Receipt letter has been received, an application for a bridging open work permit may be submitted. Since the introduction of online applications, submitting two applications together is now only accepted in very rare situations, which do not include the scenarios about which you are enquiring.
As per the Program Delivery Instructions on applying for a Bridging Open Work Permit, an application for permanent residence must have already been submitted under one of the following classes: •Federal Skilled Worker Program, Canadian Experience Class, Federal Skilled Trades Program, Provincial Nominee Program, Caring for Children Class, or Caring for People with High Medical Needs Class.
Additionally, the applicant must: currently be in Canada, have valid status on a work permit that is due to expire within four months include a copy of the Acknowledgment of Receipt letter as a supporting document.
If the permanent resident application is not complete, the bridging open work permit application will be refused and the processing fees will not be refunded.
As per the work permit application, an applicant must first determine whether they will apply on-line or on paper.
If the applicant has not yet applied for permanent residence and is therefore not eligible for a bridging open work permit, regular work permit application procedures apply. Please visit our website for further information on applying for a work permit.
Finally, if the applicant's work permit has expired within the past 90 days, they may be eligible to apply for restoration of status.
We trust this information will be of assistance.
and Cizenship Canedaot Citoyenneté Canada
Regards,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.subject: Work permit holder with a valid "V-1" visitor visa-REP-2017-2182
threads.question:
To Whom It May Concern:
An applicant, citizen, was approved for a work permit by the Vienna visa post on the basis of an inter- company transfer. At the time of issuance, she held and still holds a multiple entry "V-1" visitor visa.
The embassy in Vienna assured us that regardless of the fact that she is now a worker, she can travel to and from Canada on the "V-1" visa and re-enter as a worker as long as she continues to have the valid visa a valid work permit. However, at the port of entry, when she was issued the work permit, the CBSA officer informed her that if she wished to travel and return to Canada she would need to obtain a new counterfoil/visa indicating her status as a worker. This differs from the instructions from Vienna.
Can you please provide guidance on the correct course of action?
Thank you,
Zare.Atabak
threads.answer:
Good day,
Thank you for your enquiry and apologies for this delayed response.
In response to your question, a multiple-entry Temporary Resident Visa (TRV) continues to be valid for re-entry up to its validity date regardless of the category, even when the traveller is re-entering Canada for a different purpose. Having said this, a valid TRV does not guarantee entry to Canada. All foreign nationals must undergo an examination at the port of entry by a Border Services Officer of the Canada Border Services Agency, to determine if they are admissible to Canada.
Regards,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

You are requested to shed some light on the following scenario: We have a client who recently received an ITA based on his 2 years of Canadian work experience points. There were two claimed employments as listed below:
Employment# Four digit NOC codeFrom To
L'infora toi sur racces à infomalion 7231 - Machinists and Machining and Tooling Nov-14 Apr-16 Inspectors 7232 - Machinists and Machining and Tooling 2 Jul-17 Inspectors Dec-17
The CRS system automatically counted the months to 24 and gave the applicant points for 2 years of work experience in Canada. But when we calculate the days of employment from the exact dates, we are well short of 730 days to justify 2 years of employment in Canada. Can the applicant still apply for his permanent residency based on this ITA as this was an automatic CRS calculation or does he have to wait until he completes the 2 years, 730 days of work in Canada?
threads.answer:
Dear
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox.
Please note that our calculation is based on monthly units, and we do not take into account days. When inputting work experience "From and To" dates, the system only asks for month and year for each entry. The date range is inclusive, meaning the month in the "To" date will count towards the calculation of full time equivalent units for that particular work experience entry. Example: Using the February 1st date, and assuming the candidate worked for a year (full-time and met relevant definition of work experience), the calculation would be as follows depending on whether To Date is set to January or
February:
February 2015- January 2016 = 12 months full-time equivalent duration; February 2015- February 2016= 13 months full-time equivalent duration
In a case such as your client's, at time of assessment, the IRCC reviewing officer will use their discretion when evaluating information and supporting documents included in the application. If your client meets all other minimum requirements and the applicant indicated that the job is ongoing and they would meet work experience in the short interim, the officer may consider that this meets the work experience requirement. However, if your client prefers to be sure of the outcome s/he may decline this round of invitations and wait for future rounds once the work experience meets CEC requirement.
We trust this information will assist you.
Sincerely,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.subject: Relevant experience for a self-employed person-REP-2017-2308
threads.question:
Dear Sir/Mdm:
According to the online program instructions, relevant experience for a self-employed person means at least two years of experience during the period starting five years before the application.
For athletics, the experience must be:
a. two one-year periods being self-employed in athletics, or
b. two one-year periods participating at a world class level in athletics, or
c. a combination of a one-year period described in a above, and a one-year period described in b above.
How is the “two one-year periods participating at a world class level in athletics" interpreted?
Would it be:
a) In calendar year 2016, the applicant participated in an international competition, and in calendar year 2017, applicant participated in another international competition; or
b) In Aug 2016, applicant participated in an international competition. So, the two years will only end in Aug 2018.
Any guidance is greatly appreciated. Thank you and happy new year.
and Citizenship Caneda
Zare.Atabak
threads.answer:
Immigration Representatives / Représentants immigration
(IRCC)
Hello,
Thank you for your email to the Immigration Representatives Mailbox.
To be a member in the self-employed class, the applicant must have a minimum of two years of relevant experience in cultural activities, athletics, or the purchase and management of a farm.
In regards to relevant work experience for athletics, the requirement of "two one-year periods participating at a world class level in athletics" is interpreted as two separate one-year periods of self-employment in this area. These periods of self-employment do not have to be acquired consecutively but must have been acquired during the period starting five years before the date the application for permanent residence is received.
We trust this information will assist you.
Regards,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.subject: When is the ITA requirement needed
threads.question:
Dear Sir or Madam:
I would like to seek some clarification on the Express Entry system in the following circumstance:
and Citizenshi Canada et Ciloyeneé Canada
An individual did not misrepresent on the Express Entry profile
However, they receive a higher level of points relating to Canadian work experience than expected. This leads to an Invitation to Apply (ITA). The individual will meet the threshoid to obtain those extra Canadian work experience points within the 90 days to submit the eAPR.
Is the individual obligated to decline the ITA, because they did not meet the CRS points at the time of the ITA? OR may the individual continue to submit the eAPR within the 90 day period, once that passage of time means the individual subsequently earns those extra Canadian work experience points?
Thank you in advance for your guidance and happy new year! Yours truly,
Zare.Atabak
threads.answer:
FW: When is the ITA requirement needed-REP-2017-2317
Thank you for contacting the Immigration Representatives mailbox. We hope that you will find the answer to your question below of assistance.
Question: Is the individual obligated to decline the ITA, because they did not meet the CRS points at the time of the ITA? OR may the individual continue to submit the eAPR within the 90 day period, once that passage of time means the individual subsequently earns those extra Canadian work experience points?
Answer: When the Comprehensive Ranking System triggers an invitation to apply early, officers will look for evidence that the job is continuing or if the required work experience was obtained before the time of application. The onus remains on the applicant to demonstrate they meet the criteria under which they were invited to apply. A letter of explanation may assist the officer with the assessment of the applicant's work experience.
Please note that our calculation is based on monthly units, and we do not take into account days. When inputting work experience “From and To” dates, the system only asks for month and year for each entry. This results in some applicants being invited “early". That said, the date range is inclusive, meaning the month in the To date will count towards the calculation of full time equivalent units for that particular work experience entry. Example: Using the February 1st date, and assuming the candidate worked for a year (full-time and met relevant definition of work experience), the calculation would be as follows depending on whether To Date is set to January or February:
February 2016 - January 2017 = 12 months full-time equivalent duration February 2016 – February 2017 = 13 months full-time equivalent duration
In situations where the applicant completed or left the employment and the duration of that employment did not meet the criteria under which the candidate was invited to apply the candidate should decline the ITA and re-enter the pool.
Sincerely,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox
